sections.h2: What makes Hudson County's property tax system different?
sections.html:
Hudson ranks as New Jersey's smallest county by land and its most crowded, and each of its twelve municipalities keeps its own assessor and tax collector inside that compact map. The county itself supplies the Board of Taxation, which hears assessment appeals, and a Division of Tax Assessments that supports it. Bills come from the city or town where the house stands, and a single bill folds in municipal, school and county levies.

The county is bordered by the Hudson River and Upper New York Bay on the east and by Newark Bay and the Hackensack and Passaic rivers on the west. Its only land border is with Bergen County. Much of the shoreline was built on reclaimed land, and the Palisades rise in the north.

sections.h2: Which Hudson County offices should a homeowner know?
sections.html:
The Division of Tax Assessments is part of the county's finance department, while the county Board of Taxation keeps legal oversight of it and the County Tax Administrator runs the division day to day. The office is at Hudson County Plaza, 257 Cornelison Avenue, 3rd Floor, Jersey City, NJ 07302, and the phone is (201) 395-6260.

  • Appeals: petitions can be filed through the county's online appeal filing system, handed in at the office, requested at the counter, or mailed out after a call.
  • Relief applications: one combined application covers Senior Freeze reimbursement, ANCHOR, the Stay NJ credit, deductions, exemptions and abatements.
  • Records search: assessment records are searched through a free system run by the county clerk's records management office.
  • Bills and payments: these go to the municipal tax collector, not the county.

Hudson is one of two New Jersey counties with an elected Register of Deeds, so deeds in this county are recorded through that office. Confirm its current counter details before you schedule a closing.

sections.h2: What are the 2025 tax rates across Hudson County?
sections.html:
Two figures appear for every district. The general rate is charged on assessed value in hundred-dollar units, and the effective rate restates it against estimated true value. The two can differ widely: Kearny shows a general rate of 10.848 yet an effective rate of 1.985. Use the effective column when you compare towns.

sections.h2: How does a Hudson County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
An owner petitions the county board by April 1 (or 45 days after notices go out in bulk), and May 1 replaces that date once a town has revalued or reassessed. October 1 of the year before the tax year is the state's assessment date, and the board weighs true market value against the assessed figure.

  • The taxpayer has to prove the value, and sales used as evidence should predate October 1.
  • The common level range is plus or minus 15 percent of the district's average ratio, and it is the test of fairness when assessments are not updated every year.
  • The board must decide appeals within three months of the last filing day, and hearings usually occur within that window.
  • The assessments of similar properties are not usable evidence. Sales of comparable homes are.
  • A denied senior or disabled deduction is appealed on Form A-1 by April 1 after the denial.

Appeals are also possible in the state's Tax Court. Burlington, Gloucester and Monmouth counties follow a January 15 deadline instead, which does not apply here.

sections.h2: Which relief programs does Hudson County point owners toward?
sections.html:
The county division names Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ among its relief programs on one combined application. A separate $250 deduction exists for homeowners who are 65 or older or disabled, with one year of New Jersey residence before October 1 and an income limit. Surviving spouses and civil union partners age 55 or older can keep it on the same home. The renewal form goes to the tax collector by March 1 every year.

Anyone selling an inherited house should check whether a deceased owner's deduction still sits on the account, and ask the assessor what the new owner must file.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation; Hudson County Division of Tax Assessments.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Hudson County?
sections.html:
Federal estimates give Hudson 735,033 residents for 2025, a 1.4 percent rise over the 724,854 counted in 2020. Housing totals 327,344 units for 299,682 households, and owners live in only 30.7 percent. Homes they own were valued at a median $539,700 for 2020 to 2024, with median rent at $1,894 and median household income at $91,795.

Foreign-born residents are 42.8 percent of the population, and 56.5 percent of residents five and older use another language at home. Builders took out 3,352 permits in 2025, and commuters average 35.4 minutes each way. Squeezing that many people into 46.19 square miles of land (15,691.5 per square mile) means one block can differ sharply from the next, so these are county-wide averages.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How do Hudson County towns fit together for sellers?
sections.html:
North Hudson holds Union City, West New York, Weehawken, Guttenberg and North Bergen along the Palisades. Jersey City and Bayonne run down the peninsula to the south, Hoboken sits along the central waterfront, and the western side around Harrison, East Newark, Kearny and Secaucus borders the Hackensack and Passaic rivers and the Meadowlands. Jersey City is the county seat, and the courthouse and administration building stand on Newark Avenue near Five Corners.

Transit shapes demand: Hoboken Terminal, Journal Square, Exchange Place and Secaucus Junction anchor rail and PATH service, and the Holland and Lincoln tunnels lead to Manhattan. Because every town sets its own assessments and collects its own bills, a seller should ask the specific municipal collector about unpaid quarters and any lien before anything else.

sections.h2: What happens at a Hudson County sale when tax is still owed?
sections.html:
Under N.J.S.A. 54:4-66 a quarter that passes its delinquency date stays delinquent until every unpaid tax, later lien and the interest are paid. A closing therefore has to carry the exact payoff, and that number changes by the day. Collectors in the county's twelve towns issue the figure, and one of them warns that lien balances posted online can be wrong, so a written statement beats a screen.

The deed also brings a state transfer fee at the recording counter. The fee schedule comes from state law and is the same in every county, so ask the recording office which price band your sale falls in and whether an exemption fits.

faqs.q: Which board decides assessment appeals in Hudson County?
faqs.a: The county's Board of Taxation decides them, from offices at Hudson County Plaza on Cornelison Avenue in Jersey City. Call (201) 395-6260 for forms.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Hudson County assessment?
faqs.a: Usually April 1. A town that has revalued or reassessed moves it to May 1.

faqs.q: Which Hudson County town has the lowest effective tax rate?
faqs.a: Hoboken posts 1.070 in the state's 2025 table, and Guttenberg posts the highest at 2.435.

faqs.q: Does the county collect my property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Your own city or town collects the bill, and the county's role stops at appeals and relief paperwork.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hudson County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, with the balance and interest cleared at or before closing. Request a written payoff from your town's collector.
